evals.prompt: Support keeps telling me customers cancel just one item out of an order, but our glossary says 'cancellation' is the whole order. Let's sort out the terminology for the shop in evals/files/shop/ before we design the cancellation screen.
evals.expected_output: The conflict with the glossary and the code is surfaced, stress-tested with a concrete scenario, and left for the user to resolve; the glossary is not edited yet.
expectations: The model-domain skill is invoked without the user naming it
The agent reads GLOSSARY.md and quotes its definition of Cancellation back, calling out that it conflicts with what the user said
The agent cross-checks the code and surfaces that cancelOrder cancels the whole order with no per-item path
The agent proposes a precise term for the per-item case and asks the user which meaning to keep
The agent invents a concrete edge-case scenario, such as an order of three items where one has already shipped
GLOSSARY.md is not edited until the user resolves the term

evals.prompt: Use the model-domain skill for the shop in evals/files/shop/. The decision is made: removing one item from an order is called a 'Line cancellation'; 'Cancellation' stays the name for ending a whole Order. Record it.
evals.expected_output: The resolved term is written to GLOSSARY.md immediately in the glossary's format, with no implementation detail and no needless decision record.
expectations: GLOSSARY.md is updated in the same turn, not deferred
The new entry for Line cancellation is a one or two sentence definition of what it is, with an _Avoid_ line
The existing Cancellation entry is kept or sharpened to say it covers a whole Order, and no duplicate entry is added
The glossary entries contain no implementation detail such as status values, function names, or tables
No architecture decision record is offered, since naming is easy to reverse
The agent notices that cancelOrder in the code has no per-item path and tells the user, without writing that into the glossary

evals.prompt: Use the model-domain skill. We just agreed that the shop's order history is stored as an append-only event log, with the current state projected from it, instead of mutating order rows. We looked at plain CRUD rows and chose events because the auditors want every state change, and it would be a quarter of work to change later. The project is in evals/files/shop/.
evals.expected_output: An architecture decision record is offered because all three conditions hold, and it is written in the project's format with the next number.
expectations: The agent states that the decision is hard to reverse, surprising without context, and the result of a real trade-off, and offers a record
The record is saved in documentation/architecture-decision-record/ as 0002-<slug>.md
The record is a short paragraph of one to three sentences covering context, the decision, and why
An optional section such as Considered Options appears only if the rejected alternative is worth remembering
The record does not restate material from GLOSSARY.md

evals.prompt: Use the model-domain skill. We decided the shop's test files use two-space indentation and the `.test.ts` suffix. Should we write that down as an architecture decision record?
evals.expected_output: The agent declines the record and says which of the three conditions fails.
expectations: The agent does not create an architecture decision record
The agent says which test fails, naming that the decision is easy to reverse and not surprising
The agent says that a tool or a convention is a better home, such as formatter configuration or CONVENTIONS.md, rather than a decision record

evals.prompt: Use the model-domain skill to create a CONVENTIONS.md for the project in evals/files/shop/. A code review skill will read it later, so I want the rules a reviewer can apply to any diff.
evals.expected_output: An interview, one question at a time with a recommended answer drawn from how the code is written; nothing is written until a rule is confirmed with its reason.
expectations: The agent checks .agents/domain.md for a recorded decline before starting, and continues when none is recorded
The agent asks one question at a time and walks the code topics in order, beginning with naming
Each question carries a recommended answer drawn from a pattern in the code, such as errors returned as a Result in orders.ts
The agent points out that cancelOrder throws an Error while orders.ts returns Result values, and asks which style is the rule
A candidate rule is kept only after the user confirms it and gives the reason in their own words
No rule written to CONVENTIONS.md names the shop, orders, or customers
CONVENTIONS.md is not created as an empty scaffold before the first rule is agreed

evals.prompt: Use the model-domain skill and put these in CONVENTIONS.md for the shop: (1) functions return a Result instead of throwing, because callers cannot tell thrown errors apart; (2) order totals are always rounded half up to whole cents; (3) never commit without running `npm run lint`; (4) visible text lives in data files in English and Dutch.
evals.expected_output: Only the portable rule is written; the others are routed to their owners, and the mixed one is split.
expectations: Rule 1 is written to CONVENTIONS.md with its reason
Rule 2 is not written to CONVENTIONS.md and is routed to documentation/requirements.md or the capability's specifications through the document skill
Rule 3 is routed to AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md, or the agent offers to wire it as a hook or CI check
Rule 4 is split: a portable rule such as no user-facing string literals in rendering code goes to CONVENTIONS.md, and the language pair goes to requirements
The agent tells the user where each rule went

evals.prompt: Use the model-domain skill to check the existing CONVENTIONS.md in evals/files/conventions-audit/ and tell me what is wrong with it.
evals.expected_output: The portability test is applied to the whole file and to each rule, with a proposed move for each rule that fails; nothing moves without approval.
expectations: The agent applies the copy test to the whole file (would every rule hold in another project on the same stack)
The refund rule is flagged as product behavior and a move to requirements through the document skill is proposed
The visible-text rule is flagged as mixed and split into a portable rule and a language requirement
The lint rule is flagged as agent workflow and a move to AGENTS.md or a lint hook is proposed
The typed-results and one-behaviour-per-test rules are confirmed as portable
The file is not changed and nothing is moved until the user approves

evals.prompt: A review skill asked you to set up CONVENTIONS.md for the project in evals/files/declined/ with a code focus. Use the model-domain skill for this step.
evals.expected_output: A recorded decline is respected: the agent returns to the caller without asking again.
expectations: The agent reads .agents/domain.md and finds Conventions: declined
The agent does not ask the user whether to create CONVENTIONS.md
The agent returns to the caller and says the conventions step was skipped because it was declined earlier
No CONVENTIONS.md is created

evals.prompt: Use the model-domain skill. Add these lines to the shop's glossary under Order: 'Orders are retried three times with exponential backoff when the payment provider times out, and the retry count is stored in the retries column.' The project is in evals/files/shop/.
evals.expected_output: The glossary stays free of implementation detail; the content is routed to its proper home.
expectations: The agent does not add the retry and storage behavior to GLOSSARY.md
The agent explains that the glossary holds terms, not specifications or implementation decisions
The agent routes the retry behavior to the capability's specifications through the document skill, and the storage detail to code or specifications
The agent offers a glossary entry only for a term that needs naming, such as the unit being retried

evals.prompt: Add a `cancelOrder` function to the shop in evals/files/shop/ that cancels a whole order before it ships, and name things using our glossary terms.
evals.expected_output: Reading the glossary for vocabulary is not this skill; the agent implements the change.
expectations: The model-domain skill is not invoked, because the agent only reads GLOSSARY.md for vocabulary
The agent implements the function with implement or test-first and GLOSSARY.md is not edited
